cards.question: Core mission of the EMS Incident Commander?
cards.answer: Own the incident: command post, METHANE, objectives, assign officers, request resources, coordinate agencies — never hands-on patient care.

cards.question: Core mission of the Triage Officer?
cards.answer: Find and sort all casualties fast: global sort, tag, seconds-long LSIs, report counts to IC, direct reds to treatment, re-triage.

cards.question: What may the Triage Officer do to a patient?
cards.answer: Only seconds-long lifesaving interventions: control massive bleeding, open/position the airway, (child) rescue breaths per protocol, auto-injector, decompression if trained and protocol allows.

cards.question: Core mission of the Treatment Officer?
cards.answer: Set up and run the treatment area by category, perform secondary triage and stabilizing care, and prioritize patients for transport.

cards.question: Core mission of the Transport Officer?
cards.answer: Coordinate loading zone, call units from staging, assign destination hospitals by capacity/capability, and keep the transport log.

cards.question: Minimum fields in a transport log?
cards.answer: Triage tag number, category, transporting unit, destination hospital, departure time (plus basic injuries/age/sex if possible).

cards.question: Why not send every patient to the closest hospital?
cards.answer: It overwhelms that hospital (which also receives most self-presenters) while others sit underused — distribute by capacity and capability.

cards.question: Staging Officer's key rules?
cards.answer: Safe location with one-way access; check in every unit; crews stay with vehicles, keys in; release only on Transport's request; report available numbers to IC.

cards.question: Who speaks to hospitals during an MCI?
cards.answer: The Medical Communications Coordinator (under Transport) — one voice to hospitals/hospital coordination center.

cards.question: What happens to the dead at an MCI?
cards.answer: Left in place unless blocking access to the living; tagged, secured, out of public view; morgue manager coordinates with law enforcement/medical examiner.

cards.question: Why wear role vests?
cards.answer: Instant visual identification of who holds which role — the scene can find its officers.

cards.question: How can green patients help?
cards.answer: Under direction they can apply pressure, assist other greens, or help carry litters — and they must still be assessed and re-triaged.
